title: Reservation cadence prep notes
content:
Purpose: prep notes for quick 1:1 with Miguel (capacity lead) — align on reservation cadence, experiment timeline, and immediate follow-ups. Keep this loose; bring the short checklist to the meeting and capture decisions.

Context (quick):
- We have increasing demand from two pilot customers (PaymentsCo, DocSummarize) for guaranteed throughput in US regions.
- Current reserved fleet (globally): ~120 GPUs across 3 regions (us-west1 A100-80: 48, us-east4 A100-40: 36, eu-west1 A10G: 36).
- Spike risk windows: EOW bursts from batch jobs + weekday ML job ramp (12:00–16:00 PST).
- Last meeting: agreed to test a "soft reservation" policy (reserve 90% committed, keep 10% as burstable on-demand) and to measure tail latency under the new autoscaler.

Meeting agenda (15–20 min):
1) Quick status (2 min) — are the soft-resv experiments running? any infra blockers?
2) Short forecast readout (5 min) — run-rate vs committed, runway days at current usage, high/med/low scenarios for next 6 weeks
3) Autoscaler tuning (5 min) — cooldowns, scale step sizes, pre-warm behavior for prefetched KV caches
4) Decisions & immediate asks (3–5 min) — commit to reservation cadence and owners for actions

Key numbers I want ready: (bring short table in Slack before meeting)
- Current 7-day avg consumption: 87 GPUs (all regions).
- 95th pct peak over last 14 days: 118 GPUs (single-day peak 132).
- Safety margin target we discussed: 15% over 95th pct for first month of reservation rollouts.
- Proposed reservation cadence: bi-weekly reservations for next 6 weeks (commit increments of 10–20 GPUs depending on region signal).

Open questions / hypotheses to validate:
- Is 15% safety margin realistic given observed burst durations (mostly < 2 hrs)?
- Can we accept region-specific overcommit (e.g., burst capacity only in us-west1) to save cost?
- Does soft reservation introduce measurable cold-start latency for KV-heavy models?

Experiment plan (short):
- Miguel: enable soft-resv flag for the us-west1 pool for 2 weeks (start Mon). Track: tail latency, frequency of fallback to on-demand, cost delta. (owner: Miguel)
- Aisha: run targeted synthetic load test that mimics PaymentsCo steady-100qps + DocSummarize batch at noon; measure 95/99 lat and throughput vs baseline. (owner: Aisha)
- Claire (me): update capacity model with new 95th pct and safety margin; produce one-slide recommendation for next leadership check. Also draft a short note for Sales about expected reservation windows. (owner: Claire)

Small operational checklist (to review live):
- [ ] Confirm on-call SRE knows experiment windows (add to #dedicated-capacity ops channel)
- [ ] Ensure autoscaler bump thresholds include KV-cache warmup metric
- [ ] Tag metrics (cost & latency) with experiment id: resv-cadence-mar26
- [ ] Add runbook entry for soft-resv rollback if 99th latency > 2x baseline

Follow-ups from last sync (quick capture):
- Miguel to share raw pod eviction logs (done, in CON-4821) — looked for thrash, none found
- Aisha to try 8-bit quant test on a canary model to lower memory pressure (in progress)
- Ops asked for per-tenant request histograms; I promised to dig up synthetic traces (TODO)

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep the meeting tight — target decisions, not deep debugging.
- If Miguel wants larger commit, push for phased commit (region first, then global)
- Remember: Sales cares about predictability > lowest cost; include that phrasing in the recommendation.

Post-meeting capture template (copy into meeting notes):
- Decision: (one line)
- Rationale: (2–3 bullets)
- Owners & deadlines: (owner — date)
- Metrics to watch: (metric — threshold)
- Rollback criteria: (criteria)

Quick draft action items (fill during meeting):
- Miguel: toggle soft-resv in us-west1 and post experiment plan link by EOD.
- Aisha: finish synthetic load test and upload csv to CON-4821 by Thu.
- Claire: update capacity model and slide by next Tue; notify Sales of expectation.

Misc links I might paste in chat:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood/DEDICATED/capacity-models (note: personal draft page)
- JIRA: JIRA-DED-319 (reservation cadence epic)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/capacity-models/pull/72 (forecast changes)
